digest.lead: Anthropic is making headlines beyond tech circles today with Chris Olah's involvement in Pope Leo's new AI encyclical, marking an unprecedented intersection of AI ethics and Vatican doctrine.
digest.summary: Meanwhile, the company is preparing to release its Mythos-class models to the public, while Claude Code users got a quick fix for a bash tool regression.

stories.headline: Anthropic's Chris Olah Collaborates with Vatican on Pope's AI Encyclical
stories.summary: Anthropic's Chris Olah has participated in the development of Pope Leo's new encyclical on artificial intelligence [1][2]. This collaboration represents a notable intersection between AI research and Vatican doctrine on technology ethics.
key_points: First known collaboration between a major AI company and the Vatican on AI ethics
Chris Olah, Anthropic's co-founder and interpretability researcher, contributed to the papal document
stories.impact: This partnership could influence how religious institutions and their billions of followers approach AI adoption, while potentially shaping Anthropic's ethical frameworks through Vatican perspectives on human dignity and technology.

sources.title: The Vatican-Anthropic relationship that's reshaping the AI ethics debate

stories.headline: Anthropic Plans Public Release of Mythos-Class Models
stories.summary: Anthropic is preparing to release its Mythos-class models to the general public [1]. Details about capabilities, pricing, or timeline remain limited, but the announcement has generated interest in the developer community.
stories.impact: Public access to Mythos-class models could democratize access to Anthropic's latest AI capabilities, potentially affecting competitive dynamics in the AI model market and expanding Claude's user base.

sources.title: Anthropic to release Mythos-class models to the public

stories.headline: Claude Code v2.1.148 Fixes Bash Tool Regression
stories.summary: Claude Code v2.1.148 has been released to address a critical regression where the Bash tool was returning exit code 127 on every command for some users [1]. The issue was introduced in the previous version 2.1.147.
stories.impact: This fix restores normal bash functionality for affected Claude Code users, ensuring command execution works properly for developers relying on shell operations in their workflows.

stories.headline: Use @-mentions to give Claude Code precise file context
stories.summary: Boris Cherny, creator of Claude Code, recommends using @-mentions to point Claude at specific files instead of letting it search. This dramatically reduces token usage and improves accuracy since Claude works with the exact files you intend rather than guessing from project structure.
actionable_steps: Type @ in Claude Code to see a file picker with fuzzy search
Select the specific files relevant to your task before writing your prompt
Combine multiple @-mentions for cross-file tasks like refactoring

stories.headline: Enable PowerShell tool for Windows development workflows
stories.summary: Claude Code now includes an opt-in PowerShell tool that allows Windows users to execute PowerShell commands directly through Claude. This provides native Windows command-line access for system administration and development tasks.
actionable_steps: Update Claude Code to version 2.1.84 or later
Enable the PowerShell tool in your settings as a preview feature

stories.headline: Add session tracking header for proxy aggregation
stories.summary: Use the `X-Claude-Code-Session-Id` header in your API requests to help proxies group requests by session without needing to parse request bodies. This improves routing and monitoring capabilities when using Claude Code through proxy servers.
actionable_steps: Add the `X-Claude-Code-Session-Id` header to your Claude Code API requests
Set the header value to your session identifier
Configure your proxy to use this header for request aggregation instead of body parsing

stories.headline: Set CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER=1 to eliminate screen flickering
stories.summary: This environment variable enables flicker-free alt-screen rendering with virtualized scrollback in Claude Code v2.1.88+. It provides a smoother visual experience when Claude Code switches between screen modes during long coding sessions.
actionable_steps: Add 'export CLAUDE_CODE_NO_FLICKER=1' to your shell profile (.bashrc, .zshrc, etc.)
Restart your terminal or run 'source ~/.bashrc' to apply the change
Launch Claude Code to verify flicker-free rendering is active

stories.headline: Use visual mode in Claude Code for text selection and editing
stories.summary: Claude Code now supports vim-style visual mode (v) and visual-line mode (V) for selecting and manipulating text. This enables more efficient text editing workflows similar to vim editors.
actionable_steps: Press 'v' to enter visual mode for character-by-character selection
Press 'V' to enter visual-line mode for line-by-line selection
Use standard vim operators on your selected text
